svg.title: FinAware — Flow: Money Plan
svg.text: How the plan is worked out, previewed and saved (parts A and B), and the tools that run entirely in the browser (part C). The plan is rules, not a model: every rand it allocates can be traced to a rule.
C · In the browser only — nothing is sent to the server
• savings — Financial_Profile (left empty if never entered, not taken
• open debts with their rate and usual due day — Debts,
Chance of a missed payment — optional
Only changes the wording of the credit advice, never an amount. If the
model cannot answer, the plan is still complete.
→ the chance of missing any payment
Give every spare rand a job — in this order
1 Breathing room: 5% of income, kept back
2 Starter safety net: up to 1 month of essentials, but at most
3 Everything else → the debt with the highest interest (the
avalanche); the minimum on the rest
No debts: finish a 3-month safety net, then save
Then the debt-free date, simulated month by month, interest first
The minimum repayments are not affordable as things stand: how
many rand are missing, and what to do about the credit — no
debt-free date, because it would not be honest
What is spare, the job for every rand, the debt-free date, credit
With warnings, e.g. no essentials entered, or savings not on record
Essentials by category, and a trial income if they like
Steps 4–7 again, with the typed essentials and income
Nothing is written — the saved budget and the income on record stay
Zod: a listed category and a sensible amount for each line
one transaction: upsert each category into Budget_Item;
delete categories left out or at R0
Finds the header row by its column names: FNB-style,
Capitec-style money in / money out, or semicolons with
By keywords in the description — rent, groceries,
transport, data … — showing the word that placed it
Debt repayments, transfers and cash stay out of essentials
Moves any payment that landed in the wrong category
The average per essential category across the
Unusual-spending alerts for the latest month
Compared with the person's own earlier months — by the same day of the month, not projected to month-end
Flags a category up by half as much again and by at least R500, and any new payee
Weighs the extra against what the plan leaves spare
Reads a sentence — "Save R10 000 by December", "Build a 3-month emergency fund" — and shows the words it understood
Turns it into a monthly amount, then asks where the money comes from: the safety net or the extra debt payment — and what
that costs (e.g. debt-free 4 months later, simulated)
The next three months, day by day
Starts from the account balance the person types
Debit orders on each debt's usual due day; pay on payday, moved to the Friday before a weekend
Shows the first day the balance would go below zero
A projection that assumes this month repeats — every assumption is listed
No — there is money to spare
B · Trying figures, then saving them
